candidate.title: Hi-SCL
candidate.scope: The named Hi-SCL RNA-seq row of the assigned Illumina schematic, interpreted using the Rotem et al. 2015 drop-based implementation. The complete supplied image also shows an upper partial CytoSeq row, Drop-Seq above, and DR-Seq below; these are neighboring workflows, not alternative targets of this Hi-SCL card. The Single cell-to-poly(A) inset identifies the target rather than adding an RNA extraction step. The row has independently prepared cell-lysate and barcode-droplet inputs, a fusion junction with RT reagent addition, intact-droplet pooling, one broad cDNA synthesis/amplification block and sequencing. The scope does not expand to other assays proposed for the Hi-SCL labeling platform.

operations.label: Fuse droplets
operations.description: Merge a cell-lysate droplet with a barcode droplet and add the depicted RT buffer to the merged aqueous compartment. This is a genuine multi-input mixing operation; RT buffer is a reagent stream.

operations.label: cDNA synthesis and amplification
operations.description: The broad depicted block converts droplet-confined poly(A)+ RNA into cell-barcoded cDNA and then produces an amplified pooled DNA library. In the primary implementation, barcoded oligo(dT) primes RT inside intact droplets; only after RT is the emulsion broken. A DNA adapter is then ligated to the cDNA 3′ end to permit amplification through common priming regions. These are explanations of the broad block, not separately drawn operations.
operations.mechanism: Oligo(dT) anneals to mRNA poly(A), and reverse transcriptase extends the barcoded DNA primer; its barcode is retained at the 5′ end of cDNA. Subsequent adapter addition and PCR prepare an amplifiable DNA library.
operations.information_effect: Changes the association carrier from a droplet to a covalent barcode–transcript-derived DNA molecule; that linkage permits bulk library preparation after droplets are broken.

method_scopes.rationale: All six operations belong to the explicitly labeled Hi-SCL row. The secondary collection page has the matching Hi-SCL heading and schematic caption, and the primary paper describes the same two-emulsion merger and in-droplet RT architecture. High-throughput single-cell labeling is the expanded name of Hi-SCL, not a separate method. The collection lists similar methods and a possible associated kit, neither of which expands the diagram target or supplies a second workflow.

evidence.locator: [b00050], Results, amplification after adapter addition
evidence.quote: Consequently, all strands containing common priming regions on both ends are selectively primed and amplified by 22 cycles of PCR, producing sufficient genomic material for sequencing, as shown in Fig 2D.

evidence.locator: [b00051], Results, paired sequence readout of the barcode and represented RNA
evidence.quote: To associate each transcript with the cell from which it originates, we sequence both ends of each strand, reading the barcode sequence from one end and the RNA sequence from the other.
